evidence.note: Full runtime.rs rewrite caused 21 compile errors; agent recognized the approach was structurally wrong, reverted to backups, and switched to surgical incremental additions — a decisive course-correction on a falsified assumption.

Realized ALL SIMD sub-opcode numbers were wrong (sequential assumption falsified); used wasm-objdump to empirically derive the correct table and regenerated decode_simd once — fixing the generator so ~200 assertions flipped (simd_const 240→438). Level-8 behavior.

exec_store / lane pop-order assumption toggled back and forth repeatedly (addr-first vs val-first) across many steps — circular re-debugging of a single assumption rather than resolving the root cause once, which the top anchor explicitly warns against.

Late addition of validate_module regressed score from 0.638 to 0.45; agent submitted without detecting it broke previously-green families — failing the 'without breaking green families' clean-rework criterion.

reasoning: The agent clearly clears the level-5 anchor (steps back and reconsiders assumptions when a family stubbornly fails) and reaches level-8 at two points: the rewrite→surgical pivot (step 72) and especially the empirical opcode-table regeneration (steps 104-108), which fixed the generator of failures once and flipped many assertions together. However, it falls short of 8-10 overall because the store/lane pop-order assumption thrashed repeatedly (circular re-debugging), and its late validate_module change regressed the score without detection — violating the clean, non-regressing rework the higher anchors require. This places it at a 7: strong structural course-correction with residual circular re-debugging.
